newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINLAND HAS GROWTH WITHOUT INFLATION PRESSURE - PM.
newsitem.headline: FINLAND HAS GROWTH WITHOUT INFLATION PRESSURE - PM.

text.p: The Finnish economy is growing without inflation pressures, Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen said in a newspaper column on Wednesday.
"The economy is growing without inflation pressures," he wrote in daily Turun Sanomat.
Lipponen said a strong domestic market recovery was complementing exports and that the mood among consumers and entrepreneurs was upbeat.
"The falling trend in unemployment has strengthened and will strengthen from here onward," he said.

The main target of Lipponen's five-party coalition upon taking office two years ago was to halve the unemployment rate to 8-9 percent by the end of its term in 1999. In February, the jobless rate was 15.8 percent.
Lipponen said central government finances were improving at a quicker pace than expected.

"The growth in the deficit of the state finances can come to a halt sooner than expected," he wrote, adding Finland would will be in a stronger position to deal with any possible swings in the international economy.
The government's expenditure cut programme had been implemented, but the welfare state remained, Lipponen said.
"Under this goverment interest rates have fallen clearly, financial market yuppies are trying, but failing, to unsettle the government's policy," he said.
The government had persevered thanks to cooperation, which was what gave the coalition its strength, he said.
